items.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launched on Thursday after years of speculation about a Nintendo remaster of the 1998 N64 classic. IGN had originally called it “the biggest game of the decade,” and it still holds the highest Metacritic score ever, though critics now debate whether the faithful approach is too safe. Series producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi said enhanced graphics let them tone down scary elements that testers once found frightening, while Eiji Aonuma defended the Water Temple redesign as a deliberate move away from its reputation for being “very, very difficult.” YouTubers praised the meticulous detail and controls.
items.title: Zelda remake stays close to original, critics weigh in

items.summary: On November 7, 2026, a Link Blog post noted that requests to Datasette table pages triggered HTTP prefetch of the next page via an HTTP link header with rel=next. The author said this is bad because browsers fetch unnecessary data and render then discard whole pages for a tiny fraction of visitors who click 'next'. She found Firefox has had an issue open about it for 24 years, linked to her own 2002 blog post on the feature she had forgotten entirely.
items.title: Datasette Issue Advises Stopping Next-Link Headers for Firefox HTML Pages

items.summary: Ahead of COP31, participants signaled that faster electrification could become a focus of the event. Chris Bowen, Australia's climate change minister and this year's head of negotiations, said he would like to see a strong outcome on electrification in their presidency-led decision, and considered it a success if countries committed to raising electricity's share of final energy demand. Akshat Rathi noted that hydrocarbon shares fall from over 80% of primary energy to 65% at the final-energy stage, framing electrification as an efficiency solution. BloombergNEF reported transition investment reached $2.3 trillion last year, up 8%. Critics caution that cost and raw-material needs limit progress, with EV sales rising while global crude-oil transport demand has increased.
items.title: Wars May Spur Faster Electrification

items.summary: The United States holds over $50 billion in its Nuclear Waste Fund but lacks a permanent disposal site, with about 97,000 metric tons of spent fuel stranded at roughly 75 sites across more than 30 states. By contrast, Finland’s Onkalo repository recently earned an operating license after two decades of work. Vincent Ialenti notes that spending the money requires approval from a Congress racked by partisanship, making long-term commitments precarious.
items.title: U.S. Nuclear Waste Fund Faces Storage Gridlock

items.summary: Honda unveiled its first premium electric mountain bike, the RN0, at EICMA 2026 in Milan. Jointly developed with German maker ROTWILD, it features a proprietary carbon monocoque frame and gull-arm swingarm drawing on Honda’s motorcycle engineering. The roughly 24 kg (53 lb) multi-role e-MTB pairs FOX suspension with Shimano electronics including a new 2.3 kg drive unit rated for up to 100 Nm of torque and 750 watts of maximum output, plus a 720 Wh battery. Honda has not announced pricing but suggests it is aimed beyond the everyman rather than as an entry-level option.
items.title: Honda Unveils Its First Premium Electric Mountain Bike With ROTWILD

items.summary: A research team from Memorial University of Newfoundland designed a solar-electric propulsion system for an 11.8-meter-long, 5.8-meter-wide boat using HOMER Pro and MATLAB/Simulink modeling based on Larnaca, Cyprus conditions. The proposed array features 32 modules rated at 330 W each, providing combined capacity of 10.56 kW across approximately 62.4 m2. Researchers said the system eliminates fossil-fuel consumption while delivering a robust energy margin and avoiding greenhouse gas emissions in marine ecosystems.
items.title: Canadian Team Designs Solar-Powered Pleasure Boat

items.summary: A computational fluid dynamics study of a proposed floating photovoltaic installation at the Occhito Dam reservoir, on the Apulia–Molise border in southern Italy, found that spacing module rows about 0.5 meters apart yields the best cooling among three-row configurations. Scientists from the University of Naples Parthenope and the University of Campania Luigi Vanvitelli reported that this intermediate spacing beat both narrower and wider layouts at wind speeds of 3.5 m/s (27.16 C versus 31.07 C) and 1.5 m/s (37.02 C). The researchers caution that results are limited to a two-dimensional model, three rows, and two wind speeds, and do not translate directly into electricity generation gains.
items.title: Study Finds Optimal Spacing Improves Cooling in Floating Solar Arrays

items.summary: CleanTechnica reports that Repsol Renewables' proposed Five Creeks wind farm in Peoria County, Illinois has cleared a key approval step after months of federal delays. The project spans 27,000 acres on private land with 113 turbines and is valued at $1.5 billion. On November 6, the county board approved it by a 12-5 vote alongside 36 construction restrictions. Repsol plans to invest over $193 million in local school districts plus additional property tax revenue for libraries and road authorities. Construction permits remain pending, with completion potentially up to five years away.
items.title: Peoria County Approves $1.5 Billion Four Creeks Wind Farm

items.summary: CleanTechnica reports that BMW is offering a free charging package to buyers of the 2027 BMW i5, BMW i7 or BMW iX3 in the US. The offer, available beginning November 5, 2026, includes $500 in charging credits split between the BMW Charging Network and IONNA locations, plus a one-year IONNA membership with a 25% discount. CleanTechnica frames the credit as modest relative to EV costs, noting the i5 lease nears $750 monthly and an outright purchase reaches almost $70,000. The report links BMW's move to a broader 'free hours' trend in US grid pricing and notes continued growth in public charging despite policy uncertainty. BMW says the offer aims to make public charging simpler, more convenient and more affordable for customers.
items.title: BMW Offers $500 EV Charging Credit With New i5, i7 and iX3 Models

items.summary: The Labubu doll craze, once unstoppable, is losing momentum, and parent company Pop Mart may be running out of steam. Mega-fan Ensito left his tech job in 2024 to chase the monsters full-time, spending more than $50,000 on a collection of more than 400 Labubus. Now his viral posts struggle for reach as he shifts focus to other trends. Pop Mart reported global sales fell by as much as 50% in the three months to late September, with US revenue down at least 70%. The firm remains worth nearly $24bn despite shares falling more than 50% from their peak. Analysts warn its success may have been a single viral moment rather than sustainable growth.
items.title: Labubu Fandom Cools as Pop Mart Sales Slump

items.summary: Volkswagen released the first official teaser of a facelifted Virtus sedan, highlighting a sharper front bumper, redesigned grille, distinctive LED lighting, blue exterior shade and GT badging. Expected to launch in December 2026, the update reportedly retains separate daytime running lights instead of a full-width strip. Reports suggest an eight-speed torque-converter automatic may replace the six-speed unit on the 1.0-litre TSI engine (115 PS, 178 Nm), while the 1.5-litre TSI keeps its seven-speed DSG at 150 PS and 250 Nm; Volkswagen has not officially confirmed the transmission upgrade.
items.title: Volkswagen Teases Virtus Facelift With New Gearbox and Sportier Styling

items.summary: At EICMA 2026, Hero MotoCorp showcased the VIDA Project VXZ, a sporty electric streetfighter developed with US-based Zero Motorcycles. Its digital cluster showed 150 km of estimated range at 80% battery, implying around 188 km on a full charge, though Hero has not confirmed an official range figure or testing conditions. The concept also reveals a belt-drive system and a charging port hidden under the fuel-tank-like enclosure; motor output, price and launch date remain unannounced.
items.title: Hero Unveils VIDA Project VXZ Electric Streetfighter at EICMA 2026

items.summary: A peer-reviewed study from New York University Langone Health analyzed federal US health data and found that exposure to Dinch, a newer plasticizer replacing phthalates in food packaging, is linked to lower birth weight and fetal development complications. Each tenfold increase in Dinch exposure corresponded to a 27-gram reduction in newborn birth weight, against an average of about 3,400 grams. Up to 70% of women showed Dinch in their urine. The authors note the findings raise concerns about 'regrettable substitution,' where industry swaps one harmful chemical for another with similar risks. Lead author Leonardo Trasande called for stronger oversight and testing before market introduction. Global production rose from 25,000 tons in 2002 to 400,000 tons in 2024.
items.title: Study Links New Plastic Chemical to Lower Birth Weight

items.summary: Guardian-obtained internal documents reveal that, a year into the war in Gaza, which has killed more than 70,000 Palestinians, Israel’s military intelligence community suffered major outages and repeated system crashes from its network provider Cisco. A confidential memo drafted by Cisco warned the failures “deeply impacted customer sentiment” during national conflict. The leaked trove shows Cisco pursued new contracts with Israeli government clients as international bodies referred to Israel’s actions as genocide; in 2025, those intelligence contracts generated about $67m for Cisco over three years. Workers’ group Bridge to Humanity called the company “an instrument of genocide,” while Cisco declined comment and the IDF said it would not discuss other entities’ services.
items.title: Leaked Cisco Documents Reveal Pushed Israeli Military Network Deals Amid Gaza War

items.summary: An author compares household equities and mutual funds in 2026Q2/Q3 with 2000. Equity holdings rose about 40% versus the 60% to peak in 2000, while their share of net worth is now higher (31% vs. 26%). Citing Beach, Gamber and Moran (2025), a $3 trillion wealth reduction would cut consumption by roughly $80 billion; Q3 nominal consumption was about $22.5 trillion SAAR.
items.title: Household equity gains are modest, but a wealth drop could still dent spending

items.summary: Preliminary results from New Zealand's 2026 election left the shape of the next government uncertain, with neither the centre-right National coalition nor the opposition left bloc securing a decisive victory. On Saturday night, with nearly 100% of regular votes counted, National won 42 seats and its partners Act (13) and New Zealand First (12), while Labour took 35, ahead of National by just 0.02% in the party vote. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon called the result too close to call pending special votes, which tend toward the left. The centrist newcomer Opportunity entered parliament for the first time at 5.9%. Official results are due on 27 November, followed by weeks of possible negotiations under caretaker conventions.
items.title: New Zealand election results too close to call

items.summary: The Albanese government confirmed that Victoria Barracks in Sydney and Melbourne, plus Fort Queenscliff and RAAF Base Point Cook, will stay publicly owned despite an audit earmarking 63 underutilised sites for a $3bn sale. Campaigners, veterans and former prime ministers John Howard and Paul Keating opposed the move; defence minister Richard Marles said spending should focus on safety while Victoria Barracks holds “a special place in our nation’s history. ” The government plans to work with the Australian War Memorial to open the sites for public use after personnel vacate them.
items.title: Australia keeps four heritage defence sites public after backlash

items.summary: South Korean tourism is being reshaped by fans of K-dramas and K-pop, offering hope for communities facing population decline. Visitors now seek out filming locations, wear hanbok to recreate scenes from shows like Love in the Moonlight, and attend temple stays — a record 55,515 foreigners took part last year, though only about one in 10 identified as Buddhists. In Busan, BTS drew crowds that lifted Paradise Hotel's foreign share to roughly 70 per cent and occupancy to approximately 95 per cent during June concerts, up 46 per cent overall for the city. Yet benefits were uneven: a veteran vendor saw fewer fans than in 2022, prompting hopes to turn concert-goers into repeat visitors — including through Ami-dong's linguistic tie to BTS's ARMY fandom.
items.title: Pop Culture Drives Tourism Revival Across South Korea

items.summary: WTA tournament director Garbine Muguruza said Elena Rybakina's withdrawal from the season-ending championships was disappointing but understandable, as she needed time to recover physically. Rybakina pulled out Saturday citing unreadiness, with Marta Kostyuk taking her place in the eight-player field at Indian Wells. Despite losing star power, Muguruza stressed the round-robin format and strong depth would ensure a high-quality event.
items.title: Muguruza Defends WTA Finals Field After Rybakina Withdrawal

items.summary: Former New Zealand fast bowler Shane Bond's career was cut short by a back stress fracture from 2003. A meeting with Dr Grahame Inglis led him to undergo pars stabilisation surgery in 2004, which he described as potentially career-ending without it. Spinal surgeon Rowan Schouten called Bond 'patient zero' and has since performed the procedure on around 30 professional cricketers, becoming the world's leading authority after UK surgeons stopped offering it.
items.title: New Zealand surgeon becomes leading authority on fast bowler spinal repairs

items.summary: Explosions were heard on Iran's Qeshm Island and tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian state media reported two blasts, while the Revolutionary Guard said it lifted a self-imposed 2,000-kilometre missile range limit. The Associated Press reports Iran is reviewing Qatar-mediated proposals over its nuclear program, though officials stressed Tehran remains unwilling to negotiate until several US conditions are met.
items.title: Iran Reviews De-escalation Proposals as Explosions Rock Strait of Hormuz

items.summary: Officials said on Saturday that a gunman likely influenced by far-right ideology killed six people before police shot and arrested him, adding three more bodies were found at his home. The attack in Krakow's main square shocked Poland, which has long seen itself as safer than western European neighbors. It adds unease from October school stabbings authorities linked to extremist online content.
items.title: Six Killed in Krakow Mass Shooting by Far-Right Gunman

items.summary: On Saturday, President Donald Trump adopted a combative tone ahead of the January transfer of Congress to Democrats. He appointed friend and mixed martial arts promoter Dana White as White House press secretary and directed the Justice Department to investigate his political opponents after Republicans suffered midterm losses.
items.title: Trump Names UFC's Dana White as Press Secretary and Orders Investigations of Democrats

items.summary: The China Manned Space Agency announced that a Pakistani astronaut will join the Shenzhou-24 crewed mission as a payload specialist, marking the first foreign astronaut to visit China's space station and the first joint flight of Chinese and foreign astronauts in its history. The selection process began with an agreement signed in February 2025 between China and Pakistan. According to the agency, the astronaut will complete a short on-orbit flight before returning aboard Shenzhou-23. Input was provided by Xinhua.
items.title: Pakistani Astronaut Set for Historic China Space Station Visit

items.summary: A gunman opened fire in Krakow's historic square, killing six people and wounding sixteen. Police later found three additional bodies inside his home. The suspect, aged 25 and described as holding radical far-right views, was shot by police. Prime Minister Donald Tusk declared the shooting an act of terrorism, saying Poland has never experienced anything quite like it.
items.title: Krakow Attacker Kills Six, Three More Bodies Found at His Home

items.summary: Terrified pedestrians fled Kraków's Main Market Square on Saturday as a gunman opened fire, killing six people and injuring 16 others. Witness footage shows people running for safety amid shots and vehicles racing past shattered windows. Police said the attacker, a 25-year-old Polish citizen, fired indiscriminately from a car before exchanging shots with officers nearby; he was wounded, arrested and hospitalized. The victims included four women and two men, one British. Two police officers were also injured, one critically.
items.title: Gunman Opens Fire in Krakow Square, Killing Six

items.summary: A mass wedding in Gaza brought together about 250 couples, organised by the UAE's Operation Gallant Knight 3. The ceremony drew brides and grooms across the enclave despite continued Israeli air strikes following an October ceasefire. Organisers framed it as a celebration of love amid destruction, while health ministry figures cite more than 74,640 deaths in the war that began on 7 October 2023.
items.title: Gaza hosts mass wedding of 250 couples amid ongoing conflict

items.summary: Footage shows people taking cover as a gunman opened fire Saturday in Kraków's Main Market Square, killing six and injuring 16. Police said the attacker, a 25-year-old Polish citizen, fired indiscriminately from a car before exchanging shots with officers; he was wounded, arrested and hospitalized. Victims included four women and two men, one British. Two police were injured, one critically. The interior minister said the suspect held ultranationalist views while the defence minister called it an act of terror; investigators believe he acted alone.
items.title: Krakow Shooting Leaves Six Dead in Market Square Attack

items.summary: Media linked to Yemen's Houthi movement say that at least 25 people, including women and children, were killed in airstrikes by Saudi Arabia on al-Shariyah. Live footage from the Houthi-run Al Masirah station showed rescuers pulling bodies and injured people from the ruins. There has been no comment from the Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government. Saba news agency said the attack was carried out by Saudi Arabia, while government forces accused the Houthis of firing a missile at the site. The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed.
items.title: Houthis Claim at Least 25 Dead in Saudi Airstrike

items.summary: Ukraine's emergency services released footage showing firefighters battling fires at industrial structures after Russian strikes hit the Kyiv region. The attacks damaged energy facilities, a major bridge, and left a kindergarten severely damaged with scattered debris. Five people were reported wounded. Ukraine prepares for winter as its strained power network faces disruption from repeated targeting.
items.title: Russian Strikes Damage Kyiv Region Infrastructure and Facilities

items.summary: Police say a gunman opened fire in the historic centre of Kraków, Poland's second-largest city, killing at least six people and wounding around a dozen. Amateur footage shows people fleeing as shots ring out while cars pass through the area; other videos capture emergency services responding to broken glass and overturned chairs, with a helicopter seen flying over the scene.
items.title: Gunman Opens Fire in Kraków, Leaving at Least Six Dead

items.summary: After winning control of both chambers and several governorships in the November 3 midterm elections, US Democrats face questions about their next moves. Analyst Patrick Malone told DW that a presidential veto is not final even without a two-thirds majority, predicting bipartisan cooperation could overturn Trump's vetoes as Republicans distance themselves from him. Cory Booker urged focus on domestic issues rather than impeachment, though investigations into the administration are expected to proceed. Brandon Conradis of Bloomberg Government noted Democrats can exert pressure over funding but cannot force cabinet changes alone. Malone warned that party unity will not endure and building a governing agenda remains difficult. This article has been translated from German.
items.title: Democrats Seek Path Beyond Midterm Victory

items.summary: On 7 November 2026, Turkish foreign minister Busranur Keskinkilic and her Egyptian counterpart Busra Nur Cakmak discussed the Middle East and the Eastern Mediterranean in a phone call. The conversation concerned regional affairs across both areas.
items.title: Turkish and Egyptian Foreign Ministers Hold Phone Call on Middle East, Eastern Mediterranean

items.summary: Two skydivers died after colliding midair during a landing over the Lake Elsinore area of California on Friday, according to The New York Times. Their parachutes became entangled at an altitude of about 45 meters (148 feet). Both sustained injuries and were taken to a hospital but died despite medical intervention. Skydive Elsinore said the accident occurred during a training camp for women organized by the company. Deirdre Vickers, a spokesperson for the Riverside County Sheriff's Office, said the incident was under investigation.
items.title: Two Skydivers Killed in Midair Collision During California Training Camp

items.summary: A proposed macro-data center for AI in rural Spain near Monfarracinos has drawn fierce opposition from a neighborhood group, which accuses the conservative mayor of lacking transparency with frightened farmers. The project, rubber-stamped by the regional government of Castile and León, is backed by energy subsidiaries Edison/EDF and FRV, estimating 426 jobs. Researcher Manuel García of CSIC warns it could raise temperatures between 2ºC and 9ºC per Cambridge studies, increase noise up to 900% at night near homes, and emit as much carbon dioxide annually as 2% of Spain’s total over its expected life span of 25 years. Critics call it destructive rather than beneficial; the mayor has declined comment.
items.title: Spanish Town Opposes AI Data Center

items.summary: After Republicans lost control of Congress in Tuesday's midterms, President Donald Trump softened his anti-immigrant rhetoric and offered to negotiate with Democrats. Activists see the shift as an opportunity to reopen immigration reform debates, demanding an end to raids and legalization for more than 10 million undocumented immigrants whom the administration has targeted since mid-2025. Francisco Moreno of COFEM urges action ahead of the 40th anniversary of Reagan's 1986 amnesty, which he says lifted incomes by an average of 15% within six years and boosted women's earnings by 21%. Activists point to H.R. 4393, the Dignity Act introduced in July 2025, as a possible path forward, though Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin warned that deportations would continue.
items.title: Activists Push for Immigration Relief After Democrats Win Midterms

items.summary: In an interview with the Guardian ahead of her memoir Belonging, Sonia Gandhi said imposing India's 1975 Emergency was a mistake and that her mother-in-law Indira Gandhi eventually came to feel likewise. She recalled crying over Babri Masjid's demolition in December 1992 and acknowledged party failures helped rise BJP Hindutva politics.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Calls Emergency a Mistake Indira Eventually Agreed

items.summary: Maya, an elephant calf found alone as a newborn on a riverbank near Kaprikkad on Apr 19, 2025, was airlifted from Keralam to Vantara's hospital in Jamnagar on Nov 5. Fractures in both front legs left her unable to stand after more than a year of care. Acting on an initiative by Anant Ambani and following a transfer order from chief wildlife warden P Pugazhendi, Vantara deployed a veterinary team; advisers identified a possible parathyroid-related disorder that may respond to treatment.
items.title: Elephant Calf Airlifted for Life-Saving Treatment

items.summary: A strong earthquake struck near Japan's Aichi Prefecture, with the Meteorological Agency rating it magnitude 5.7 and the US Geological Survey reporting magnitude 5.5. Smaller aftershocks followed, affecting a wide area including Hamamatsu, Kyoto, Nara, Yamanashi, and Gifu. The quake occurred at 1:04 am local time about 40 km below Shizuoka Prefecture's surface.
items.title: Japan Records Strong Earthquake Near Aichi Prefecture

items.summary: US President Donald Trump said he offered the vacant White House Press Secretary job to Dana White, president and CEO of the Ultimate Fighting Championship, in a Truth Social post. The role is open after Katie Zacharia was fired on October 16 following five days in it. White confirmed he would meet Trump on Monday but did not say what they discussed or whether he was seriously considering the position. Trump also asked White to bring UFC fighters, naming Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov and Justin Gaethje among others. The offer comes amid wider administration changes after midterm election losses.
items.title: Trump Offers UFC Chief Dana White a Press Secretary Role

items.summary: An author reflects ten years after Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the withdrawal of 86% of cash in November 2016. The article argues demonetisation failed its stated goals: more than 99.3% of notes returned to banks, and no major investigations followed reported suspicious transactions. Independent estimates place Covid-19 deaths at around 4 million Indians, which the author links partly to government carelessness. Digital payments via UPI grew sharply, but NEFT value in 2025-’26 remained 60% higher than UPI’s Rs 502 lakh crore versus Rs 314 lakh crore. The currency-GDP ratio stayed stable around 12%, and the Rs 500 denomination still accounts for 85.5% of notes in circulation. The author concludes demonetisation had little lasting effect on cash usage or black money, while institutional failures persisted.
items.title: Ten Years After Demonetisation, Critics Call It a Failure

items.summary: The internationally recognised Yemeni government has urged Lebanon to take coordinated and decisive action against Hezbollah's alleged military support for the Houthi militia. Foreign minister Afrah Al-Zouba, in a post on X dated November 4, welcomed Lebanon's position supporting Yemen's sovereignty while calling for joint efforts between security agencies to disrupt militant networks. Her remarks followed a statement by the Lebanese Presidency after President Joseph Aoun and Prime Minister Nawaf Salam met ahead of a Cabinet session. Salam warned against dragging Lebanon into renewed regional conflict, condemning Lebanese groups operating abroad and affirming that decisions on war must remain with constitutional institutions.
items.title: Yemen Urges Lebanon to Act Against Hezbollah Support for Houthis

items.summary: A Singapore-based software executive, Paramjith Dhankhar, was shot dead at his family residence in Faridabad late Friday after a months-long dispute with neighbours over a German Shepherd dog defecating in the parking and damage to an entrance gate. Police say suspect Mohan Sharma fired 15-19 rounds; relatives report nine hits. Sharma, arrested Saturday from Ballabgarh, was charged under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita sections including murder, with his wife and two children named for criminal conspiracy but not yet arrested. An FIR names all four at Surajkund police station on Saturday. Police say the handgun holster and magazines were recovered near where he shot Dhankhar dead before being rushed to a hospital where doctors declared him dead on arrival. Senior officers said Dhankhar tried to save himself as fire came from close range, with multiple bullet marks on his Mahindra XUV 7XO and surrounding walls. Debashish Karmakar reported for Hindustan Times.
items.title: Singapore-Based Executive Killed in Faridabad Parking Dispute

items.summary: Rohit Sharma became the batter with the most sixes against New Zealand in ODIs, surpassing Shahid Afridi's record of 50 during India's second ODI at Hnry Stadium in Wellington. He reached the milestone with two sixes off Kyle Jamieson to finish on 23 from 28 deliveries while chasing 135. The rain-affected match ended as a four-run victory for India under DLS, extending their series lead to 2-0.
items.title: Rohit Sharma Sets ODI Six Record vs New Zealand

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended Diwali greetings to people across India on Sunday, sharing a 50-second video message in which he wished everyone happiness, peace and prosperity. He reaffirmed his tradition of celebrating the festival with jawans, describing spending time among armed forces personnel as his regular routine every year that will continue this year too. The article notes these annual visits to military locations have been a consistent feature of his tenure since 2014, beginning at Siachen Base Camp and continuing across Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Rajasthan, Gujarat and aboard the aircraft carrier INS Vikrant in 2025. Modi remarked that the festival reflects resolve against darkness.
items.title: Modi Extends Diwali Greetings and Reaffirms Annual Visits to Troops

items.summary: The Federal profiles Azam Khan, a Samajwadi Party veteran whose prolonged incarceration and party isolation symbolize the decline of assertive Muslim politics in Uttar Pradesh. Since February 2020 he has spent more than five years in jail amid repeated prosecutions over cases including dual PAN cards and alleged irregularities at Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, which he founded in Rampur. SP insiders say his combative style and minority-rights focus made him a convenient target for BJP narratives; analysts describe his role as increasingly symbolic rather than organizational.
items.title: Azam Khan as Symbol of UP Political Realignment

items.summary: The Supreme Court, in Union of India v. Rohith Nathan (Justices P.S. Narasimha and R. Mahadevan), clarified how to implement its March 11, 2026 judgment on the OBC creamy layer. The order protects completed appointments but allows pending claims to be examined, applies the creamy-layer interpretation to service allocation for candidates selected in the Civil Services Examination, 2025 (results declared March 6, 2026), and leaves government equivalence exercises open-ended rather than imposing a timetable. It also addresses how parental employment status affects income thresholds under the 1993 Office Memorandum.
items.title: Supreme Court clarifies OBC creamy-layer rules for pending claims and 2025 exam

items.summary: At least seven people were injured when a fire broke out at a firecracker shop in Panruti taluk of Tamil Nadu's Cuddalore district late Saturday evening, according to district administration officials. The Fire and Rescue Services department, police and revenue officials responded and brought the situation under control. All seven injured persons were taken to the Panruti Government Hospital for first aid; two are reported critical with burn injuries covering more than 80 per cent of their bodies and may be referred to Chennai.
items.title: Seven Injured in Firecracker Shop Blaze in Cuddalore

items.summary: President Donald Trump struck a combative tone Saturday after Republicans lost control of both chambers in the midterm elections, offering UFC head and loyal supporter Dana White the White House press secretary job. In a social media post, Trump urged White to take the role while describing him as a "violent fighter." He also ordered the Justice Department to investigate Democrats over alleged extortion at the highest level. The pugilistic posts recalled remarks after his 2018 midterm defeat and subsequent impeachments in 2019 and 2021.
items.title: Trump Offers UFC's Dana White Press Secretary Role Amid Post-Election Attacks on Democrats

items.summary: President Donald Trump offered UFC chief Dana White a top job as White House press secretary, following the recent firing of Katie Zacharia after less than a week. The article provides biographical background on White's upbringing in South Boston and his career building Ultimate Fighting Championship before joining Meta's board in January 2025.
items.title: Trump Offers UFC Chief Dana White Press Secretary Role

items.summary: A farmer, Devidas Takle, was mauled to death by a tiger while collecting fodder for his cattle near Beed on Saturday. The incident occurred amid severe regional drought that pushed farmers into forest areas seeking livestock feed. Villagers have renewed demands for the animal's capture and stronger preventive measures against repeated attacks.
items.title: Drought-Driven Farmer Killed by Tiger While Gathering Fodder in Maharashtra

items.summary: The Mumbai Sessions Court refused bail to Mihir Shah, son of a Palghar politician, in the 2024 BMW hit-and-run case. On July 7, 2024, he allegedly rammed his car into a scooter carrying Pradip Nakhwa and Kaveri; she was dragged about 1.5 km on the bonnet and died. Shah's lawyer argued he had been jailed since 2024, but Public Prosecutor Ashwini Rayakar opposed it, citing High Court guidance to wait for eyewitness testimony. The court kept charges framed and ordered faster witness examination.
items.title: Sessions Court Denies Bail To Mihir Shah In Worli Hit-And-Run Case

items.summary: The Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority is restricting new compound walls around developments in Bandra-Kurla Complex (BKC) to improve pedestrian access and restore the district's original walkable-planning vision. The move follows a JLL report projecting BKC office stock to grow 32 per cent, from 20.4 million sq ft in 2026 to 26.9 million sq ft by 2029. MMRDA is urging existing establishments to voluntarily remove walls rather than dismantle barriers previously permitted.
items.title: MMRDA Bans New Compound Walls in BKC to Boost Walkability

items.summary: Ritesh Menon's Netflix film Dilwali Diwali rests on a solid idea about an engineer in Norway who buys Mumbai property his family prefers to leave. The reviewer notes it runs for a mere 61 minutes, so the complaint is that it is too short to realise its ambitions. Themes of gentrification and class insecurity remain at the level of promise rather than full exploration.
items.title: Dilwali Diwali review finds ambition outpaced by brevity

items.summary: An Indian Air Force IL-76MD heavy-lift transport aircraft, nicknamed 'Gajraj', landed at Nyoma airbase in eastern Ladakh on Friday at 13,629 feet (sentence s0), setting a world record for the highest-altitude landing by an aircraft of its class. The IAF described it as
items.title: IAF IL-76 Sets World Record for Highest Heavy Transport Landing

items.summary: A woman identified as Sanmati Majhi allegedly attacked a judicial magistrate, an assistant public prosecutor and a court security guard with an iron rod at Jharigam JMFC court in Nabarangpur district, Odisha, on Saturday. The assault injured all three; the APP was seriously hurt and hospitalized. Prosecuting officer Pradeep Patnaik recounted that Majhi had sought financial help amid a pending matrimonial dispute.
items.title: Woman Allegedly Attacks Magistrate, Prosecutor and Guard with Iron Rod in Odisha Court

items.summary: In an interview with The Hindu ahead of her memoir Belonging, Congress chairperson Sonia Gandhi said the party has nothing to learn from the BJP or RSS. She criticized PM Narendra Modi's government for damaging India's democratic fabric over 12 years, while expressing optimism that proper governance could be restored in time.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Criticizes Modi Government Over India's Democratic Fabric
